summary: Practise tourism data analysis, seasonality measures and destination monitoring. Explore the five-day foundation course and plan your learning.
lede: Tourism research and analytical methods help destination teams turn visitor data into evidence for planning. For tourism analysts, statisticians and planners, the foundation course practises framing research questions, checking data quality and selecting comparable measures. Learners also calculate seasonality, summarize visitor expenditure in Excel and prepare concise evidence briefs that communicate data limitations and uncertainty.
audienceIntro: This foundation course suits people who work with tourism activity data or use it to plan destination services. It is designed for tourism professionals who need practical ways to assess visitor patterns, explain data limitations and prepare evidence for planning discussions.
modules: Tourism Research Questions and Destination Decisions
GSTC Destination Criteria and Pressure Indicators
Excel Tourism Data Quality and Analysis
Tourism Evidence Briefing and Action Plan
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Basic familiarity with tourism operations or destination services is useful. No prior research-methods training or programming experience is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access for the spreadsheet exercises.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
